chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: George Wein and the Phil Porter organ trio
summary: Wein books him, and he builds a trio with Phil Porter and Candy Finch.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: At this time you couldn't stay with Duke, so what did you do then?
Well, just by chance... Who's the guy who used to work with George Wein?

No, not Charlie Bourgeois. An Englishman. I can't think of it... He was up in Boston when I first got in touch with George. In fact, he told me that he was responsible for me getting that tight with George.
Yeah, an English cat from England. I was trying to think of his name, but I can't think of it.
But anyway, we go... What was this guy's name...?
Well, we'll get back to it, we'll think of it, and we'll put it in.
Yeah, if I can think of it! Ha-ha... Now, what were we saying?

Well, George Wein called me, you know, and he asked me if I would be interested in doing some gigs with him. So I said, 'Yeah, sure, why not?' Work for him, I might as well. I wasn't doing anything with anybody else. So he said, 'Well, what do you want to work with?' I had heard Phil Porter up in Boston, because I had worked with him on a one-night thing, and he... Jimmy Tolliver had the band up there. So he got Phil to play in his organ player's place, because it was his band, really, and I was just the added attraction for the week. So he hired me and Phil and a drummer to play a gig, because he had another gig to make in Boston. That's how I met Phil.

So when George asked me what I wanted to do, what I wanted to work with, I thought about Phil. I said, 'Well, I'd like to get this little organ player and get myself organized when there was a trio,' because it would be easy to work in a trio and I could work in any type of club, whereas there don't have to be a whole lot of money for me
to be dealing with, and I could still give the guys a decent salary and make a decent salary for myself.
